title_en: Supreme People's Court Publishes Seven Model Cases on Protecting People's Livelihood
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Publication of Seven Typical Cases on Safeguarding People's Livelihood

I. Retrial Applicant: Villagers' Committee of Xunfeng Village, Xunfeng Town, Xiuwu County, Henan Province v. Respondent: Xue Haijin — Dispute over Contract for Undertaking

(1) Basic Facts

On December 30, 2009, Xue Haijin entered into a contract for undertaking with the Villagers' Committee of Xunfeng Village, Xunfeng Town, Xiuwu County, Henan Province (hereinafter referred to as the Xunfeng Village Committee) to undertake the fox farm in the industrial zone north of Xunfeng Village for fox breeding, with a term of six years. During the performance of the contract, the land used by Xue Haijin's fox farm was required to be requisitioned and relocated due to project development. On March 5, 2011, without reaching an agreement on relocation compensation costs between the parties and in the absence of Xue Haijin, the Xunfeng Village Committee carried out a forced relocation of Xue Haijin's fox farm, causing losses to Xue Haijin.

(2) Judgment

At the second instance, the Henan High People's Court held that Article 7 of the contract for undertaking between the Xunfeng Village Committee and Xue Haijin stipulated that during the term of the contract, if Xue Haijin encountered policy projects at a higher level, he should comply with the planning. According to this stipulation, the land of Xue Haijin's fox farm fell within the overall planning scope of Xiuwu County's industrial cluster, which met the conditions for rescission of the contract as agreed upon by both parties, and the Xunfeng Village Committee had the right to rescind the contract. However, the Xunfeng Village Committee should have notified Xue Haijin and, based on the normal breeding needs of the fox farm, given Xue Haijin a reasonable period for relocation. Since no agreement was reached between the parties, the Xunfeng Village Committee, without granting Xue Haijin a reasonable relocation period, unilaterally carried out a forced relocation, constituting a tort, and should bear corresponding tort liability for compensation. In its second-instance judgment, the court ordered the Xunfeng Village Committee to compensate Xue Haijin for losses of fox stock amounting to over RMB 3.5 million. The Xunfeng Village Committee, dissatisfied, applied to the Supreme People's Court for retrial. The Supreme People's Court held that even if the Xunfeng Village Committee had the right to rescind the contract as agreed, it should have exercised that right in accordance with the law. Without reaching an agreement between the parties, the Xunfeng Village Committee failed to give Xue Haijin a reasonable relocation period and instead unilaterally carried out a forced relocation, causing losses to Xue Haijin, for which it should compensate. The court ruled to dismiss the Xunfeng Village Committee's application for retrial.

(3) Typical Significance

This case concerns the protection of the interests of a vulnerable relocated livestock farmer. Currently, incidents of forced relocation through violent means infringing on the interests of the public occur from time to time across various regions. Some local governments believe that when victims assert their rights, they undermine the overall stability, and that residents' failure to cooperate with relocation hinders development. Appeasing wrongdoers for the sake of maintaining stability, or infringing on public interests for the sake of temporary development, runs counter to General Secretary Xi Jinping's remarks on "implementing the basic strategy of governing the country according to law and accelerating the building of a socialist country under the rule of law." The "stability" achieved at the cost of fairness and justice is merely temporary and will inevitably trigger new instability; the "development" that infringes on public interests severs the close bond between the Party and the people, and such development—neither benefiting nor serving the people—is unsustainable. In reviewing this case, the court closely adhered to the goal of "treating the demands of the people fairly and in accordance with the law, and striving to let the people feel fairness and justice in every judicial case." It protected the vulnerable group without engaging in reverse discrimination, actively explored rules for the allocation of the burden of proof in relocation and demolition tort cases, carefully ascertained facts in light of objective laws and economic principles, and emphasized science, reason, and the rule of law. This demonstrates that only fairness and justice can safeguard the overall stability of society, and only by unswervingly implementing the mass line can sustainable development be achieved.

II. Yang Jikang (pen name Yang Jiang) v. Zhongmao Shengjia International Auction Co., Ltd. and Li Guoqiang — Pre-litigation Injunction Case

(1) Basic Facts

This case arose from a dispute over the auction of handwritten letters of the late renowned scholar Qian Zhongshu. Applicant Yang Jikang stated: Qian Zhongshu (deceased) and Yang Jikang were husband and wife, and they had a daughter, Qian Yuan (deceased). Qian Zhongshu, Yang Jikang, and Qian Yuan were friends with Li Guoqiang. The three had successively sent over a hundred private letters to Li Guoqiang, which were originally kept by Li Guoqiang. However, in May 2013, Zhongmao Shengjia Company issued an announcement stating that it would hold a public auction of "Also a Collection—Handwritten Letters of Qian Zhongshu" on June 21, 2013, to auction off these private letters. In preparation for this auction, Zhongmao Shengjia Company also planned to hold a related seminar on June 8, 2013, and a preview exhibition from June 18 to 20, 2013. Yang Jikang contended that Qian Zhongshu, Yang Jikang, and Qian Yuan each held copyright in the letters they had written. Qian Yuan and Qian Zhongshu passed away on March 4, 1997, and December 19, 1998, respectively. After Qian Zhongshu's death, the property rights in his copyright were inherited by Yang Jikang, while his moral rights of authorship, right of revision, and right of integrity were to be protected by Yang Jikang, and his right of publication was to be exercised by Yang Jikang. After Qian Yuan's death, the property rights in her copyright were jointly inherited by Yang Jikang and Yang Weicheng (Qian Yuan's spouse), while her moral rights of authorship, right of revision, and right of integrity were to be protected by Yang Jikang and Yang Weicheng, and her right of publication was to be jointly exercised by Yang Jikang and Yang Weicheng. Given that Yang Weicheng expressly stated he would not assert his rights in this case, Yang Jikang was entitled to assert the relevant rights in accordance with the law. Yang Jikang claimed that the upcoming public auction of private letters by Zhongmao Shengjia Company and Li Guoqiang, as well as the ongoing public exhibition and promotion activities, would infringe on the copyright that Yang Jikang owned and inherited. If such conduct were not promptly stopped, it would cause irreparable harm to Yang Jikang's lawful rights and interests. Therefore, she applied to the court for an order to require Zhongmao Shengjia Company and Li Guoqiang to immediately cease the public auction, public exhibition, and public promotion of the private letters over which Yang Jikang held copyright.

(2) Judgment

The Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court, based on the provisions on preservation of acts under the amended Civil Procedure Law, issued an injunction: Zhongmao Shengjia International Auction Co., Ltd. was prohibited from engaging in acts during the auction, preview, and promotion activities that would infringe on the copyright in the handwritten letters in question written by Qian Zhongshu, Yang Jikang, and Qian Yuan to Li Guoqiang, including through public publication, exhibition, reproduction, distribution, or dissemination via information networks. After the order was served, Respondent Zhongmao Shengjia Company immediately issued a statement, "deciding to cancel the public auction of 'Also a Collection—Handwritten Letters of Qian Zhongshu' scheduled for June 21, 2013."

(3) Typical Significance

This case is the first interim injunction concerning copyright moral rights issued by a people's court, and also the first interim injunction issued against copyright infringement after the implementation of the Civil Procedure Law (Revised in 2012). Moreover, because the case involved the late renowned Chinese writer and literary scholar Mr. Qian Zhongshu and the famous Chinese writer, translator, and foreign literature scholar Ms. Yang Jiang, it attracted widespread social attention. The trial court actively and reasonably adopted preservation measures, accurately grasping the applicable conditions and procedures for such measures, thereby providing timely protection to the rights holder while preventing abuse of litigation rights. At a time when all sectors of society were highly concerned about the imminent large-scale exposure of Qian Zhongshu's manuscripts, the court fully considered the potential impact of the case on the public interest and accurately issued a judicial injunction. This effectively protected the copyright holder's rights while avoiding adverse effects on the auction company and the relevant public. The injunction helped promote the protection of the copyright and privacy rights of letter writers by recipients across society, demonstrated judicial authority, and fulfilled the social guidance function of the judiciary.

III. Series of Disputes Arising from the Abandonment of the Sierra Leone-Flagged Vessel "LEDOR" by Its Albanian Owner, Genie Maritime Services Ltd.

(1) Basic Facts

The Sierra Leone-flagged vessel "LEDOR," carrying 20,000 tons of imported iron ore for a large Chinese state-owned enterprise, ran aground off Putian, Fujian Province, in October 2011 while en route from Chennai Port, India, to Nantong Port, Jiangsu Province, China. The maritime authority deemed that the vessel posed risks of breaking apart, sinking, endangering human life, and polluting the marine environment. It required the shipowner to submit a vessel salvage plan, measures for lightering the cargo and the oil on board, while the consignee demanded that the shipowner discharge the cargo at the site, but neither party complied. The local government, aiming to protect the environment and ensure safety, repeatedly coordinated and mobilized to have the vessel berth and discharge cargo, but failed due to various practical issues that remained unresolved. The vessel was old, with damaged ballast tanks and partial cargo holds, and its certificates had expired. The Albanian owner, Genie Maritime Services Ltd., was unable to make the vessel seaworthy and subsequently abandoned the vessel, along with over a dozen foreign crew members and the cargo, in Putian, Fujian. In July 2012, the consignee applied to the Xiamen Maritime Court for a maritime injunction and maritime claims preservation, seeking to seize the vessel and compel the discharge of cargo. While the Xiamen Maritime Court was executing the civil ruling, the Albanian captain and 17 Syrian crew members stated that they would not allow the vessel or cargo to leave their control until their substantial outstanding wages were paid. After extensive communication, the 18 foreign crew members agreed to file a lawsuit through legal channels to demand the shipowner pay their wages. Subsequently, the consignee sued Genie Maritime Services Ltd. for compensation for cargo losses, etc. Farmers whose aquaculture operations had been damaged by the "LEDOR" grounding, as well as various companies that had provided anti-pollution services, supplies of materials and fuel oil, and agency services to the vessel during its stranding, also filed lawsuits demanding payment of relevant fees, thereby giving rise to a series of major, complex, and difficult cases of various types.

(2) Judgment

After accepting the above cases, the Xiamen Maritime Court contacted the shipowner through various channels, but the shipowner, heavily indebted, had neither the intention nor the capacity to address the disputes. On one hand, the Xiamen Maritime Court promptly and lawfully ordered the auction of the vessel, issued public announcements, and notified relevant creditors to register their claims. Given the extremely sluggish shipping market, the vessel failed to sell at two public auctions. The court then tried every means to contact potential buyers, ultimately selling the vessel at a high price exceeding the shipowner's estimate. On the other hand, the court promptly conducted open trials of the series of disputes arising from the "LEDOR" in accordance with legal procedures. In the absence of the defendant, who failed to appear or submit any evidence, the court thoroughly investigated the debts and claims arising from the vessel's stranding in Putian by visiting multiple agencies including the port authority, quarantine, customs, border inspection, maritime authority, and pilot station in Putian Port. It carefully scrutinized and verified various types of evidence and ultimately rendered first-instance judgments, equally protecting the lawful rights and interests of Chinese and foreign parties. After service by public notice, the series of first-instance judgments became legally effective in May 2013. Subsequently, the Xiamen Maritime Court timely convened a creditors' meeting and distributed the proceeds from the vessel auction in accordance with legal provisions. Considering that Syria was subject to economic sanctions by Western countries, and to ensure the timely and accurate payment of wages to the crew, the Xiamen Maritime Court contacted the crew via email and remitted the wages to their designated accounts in third countries.

(3) Typical Significance

When executing the arrest warrant and maritime injunction, the Xiamen Maritime Court learned that the crew had been abandoned by the shipowner on board without basic living security and with impaired physical and mental health. The court designated a state-owned ship agent to provide ship agency services for the "LEDOR," offered full humanitarian assistance to the crew, arranged funds through multiple channels to supply the vessel and crew, and even arranged Ramadan meals for the Syrian crew. When crew members fell ill, the court coordinated with the Putian municipal government to arrange for medical personnel to provide medical services. It also coordinated with the foreign exchange control department to handle matters on a case-by-case basis, converting the RMB wages advanced by the consignee into US dollars for distribution to the crew. These efforts not only effectively induced the foreign crew to cooperate with the court in executing the maritime injunction and arrest order, but also demonstrated the fair and efficient work style of Chinese courts and a humanitarian, internationalist spirit. Finally, the Xiamen Maritime Court also contacted the public security department to handle the appropriate visas and exit procedures for these foreign crew members based on their special circumstances, enabling them to return to their home countries in batches. The Syrian crew presented a banner to the Xiamen Maritime Court inscribed in English with the words "People's Judges for the People," and the Syrian Embassy in China sent a letter of thanks to the Xiamen Maritime Court. The Xiamen Maritime Court thus accumulated valuable experience in adjudicating this series of major, complex, difficult, and typical cases when a foreign shipowner had abandoned the vessel.

IV. Fan Gensheng v. People's Government of Jiashan County, Zhejiang Province — Administrative Reconsideration on Environmental Protection

(1) Basic Facts

Since 2002, Fan Gensheng had been engaged in aquaculture utilizing a 60-mu (approx. 4 hectares) water area at Bailongtan in Ganyao Town, Jiashan County. On November 20, 2012, Fan Gensheng sent a letter to the Jiashan County Environmental Protection Bureau, complaining about severe river pollution and damage to his aquaculture operations. He requested that the competent authority diligently perform its duties, investigate and address the matter in accordance with the law, compensate for losses, and take specific administrative actions. The letter stated that since May 2012, some individuals had been raising pigs and operating a dishware washing plant, discharging wastewater into the river, causing serious water pollution and massive fish mortality. On November 21, 2012, the Jiashan County Environmental Protection Bureau received Fan Gensheng's complaint letter. On December 31, 2012, Fan Gensheng applied for administrative reconsideration to the People's Government of Jiashan County, seeking an order to require the Jiashan County Environmental Protection Bureau to perform its statutory duties. On February 26, 2013, the Jiashan County People's Government issued an administrative reconsideration decision ([2013] No. 5), holding that Fan Gensheng's application for administrative reconsideration, on the ground that the Jiashan County Environmental Protection Bureau had failed to perform its statutory duties after receiving his complaint, fell within the scope of acceptance for administrative reconsideration. Article 22, Paragraph 2 of the State Council's Regulations on Letters and Visits provides that upon receiving a letter or visit matter, the relevant administrative organ shall, if it can immediately respond whether to accept it, provide a written response on the spot; if it cannot respond immediately, it shall inform the petitioner in writing within 15 days from the date of receiving the letter or visit matter. The respondent, Jiashan County Environmental Protection Bureau, failed to submit evidence demonstrating that it had registered and accepted Fan Gensheng's letter/visit matter. Therefore, it was deemed that the respondent had accepted the letter/visit matter. Article 33 of the Regulations on Letters and Visits provides that a letter/visit matter shall be concluded within 60 days from the date of acceptance; if the situation is complex, the handling period may be appropriately extended, but the extension shall not exceed 30 days, and the petitioner shall be informed of the reasons for extension. The respondent, Jiashan County Environmental Protection Bureau, received the letter/visit application on November 21, 2012. As of December 31, 2012, when Fan Gensheng applied for administrative reconsideration, the handling period under the Regulations on Letters and Visits had not yet expired. Article 16, Paragraph 1 of the Implementing Regulations of the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where a citizen, legal person, or other organization applies to an administrative organ for it to perform statutory duties, and the administrative organ fails to do so, the time limit for applying for administrative reconsideration shall be calculated from the following dates: (1) if there is a specified period for performance, from the day after the expiration of that period. Therefore, the time limit for applying for administrative reconsideration in this case should be calculated from the expiration of the period specified in the Regulations on Letters and Visits. Accordingly, Fan Gensheng's application for administrative reconsideration did not meet the requirement under Article 28, Item (4) of the Implementing Regulations of the Administrative Reconsideration Law, as it was not filed within the statutory time limit. In accordance with Article 48, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (2) of the Implementing Regulations of the Administrative Reconsideration Law, the government decided to dismiss Fan Gensheng's application for administrative reconsideration. Fan Gensheng, dissatisfied with this reconsideration decision, filed a lawsuit with the Jiashan County People's Court, alleging that the administrative reconsideration decision made by the People's Government of Jiashan County was procedurally unlawful, factually incorrect, and legally erroneous, and that it had led to the expansion of his losses. He requested the court to revoke the administrative reconsideration decision ([2013] No. 5), order the defendant to render a new reconsideration decision, and order the defendant to compensate him for the losses caused during the period of intentional delay.

(2) Judgment

On May 21, 2013, the Jiaxing Intermediate People's Court rendered the administrative judgment ([2013] Zhe Jia Xing Chu Zi No. 2), ordering: (1) the revocation of the administrative reconsideration decision ([2013] No. 5) of the People's Government of Jiashan County; (2) the People's Government of Jiashan County to render a new specific administrative act within the statutory time limit from the effective date of this judgment; (3) the dismissal of Fan Gensheng's other claims. Fan Gensheng, dissatisfied, appealed to the Zhejiang High People's Court. Upon trial, the Zhejiang High People's Court held that this case was a lawsuit directly against the administrative reconsideration decision of the respondent, the People's Government of Jiashan County. The respondent contended that the complaint matter submitted by the appellant to the Jiashan County Environmental Protection Bureau fell within the scope of letters and visits matters, and that the bureau had not yet exceeded the handling period under the Regulations on Letters and Visits after receiving the complaint. Therefore, the appellant's direct application for administrative reconsideration did not meet the acceptance conditions for administrative reconsideration, and accordingly, the respondent dismissed the appellant's application for administrative reconsideration. Consequently, the focus of the trial was whether the appellant's complaint matter constituted a letter/visit matter or an application for performance of statutory duties. Article 2 of the State Council's Regulations on Letters and Visits provides that matters where a petitioner reflects circumstances, makes suggestions, opinions, or complaint applications to people's governments at all levels or to working departments of people's governments at or above the county level constitute letter/visit matters. Article 8, Paragraph 1 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Prevention and Control of Water Pollution provides that the environmental protection authority of a people's government at or above the county level shall exercise unified supervision and management over the prevention and control of water pollution. Articles 27 and 69 of the same law provide that the environmental protection authority and other departments exercising supervision and management powers under this law have the right to conduct on-site inspections of pollutant-discharging units within their jurisdiction; if they discover illegal acts or receive reports of illegal acts but fail to investigate and handle them, or otherwise fail to perform their duties under this law, the directly responsible supervisors and other directly responsible personnel shall be subject to disciplinary sanctions in accordance with the law. The Jiashan County Environmental Protection Bureau's published work responsibilities, items (3) and (6) on its website, also clearly state that it is responsible for supervising and managing the prevention and control of pollution of the atmosphere, water bodies, soil, etc., and for carrying out environmental protection administrative law enforcement inspections. In this case, the appellant's complaint alleged that relevant entities were directly discharging wastewater from pig farming and dishware sterilization into the river, causing serious water pollution and resulting in the massive death of fish and pearl mussels he was raising. He therefore requested that the respondent perform its duties and investigate and handle the matter in accordance with the law. Viewed from the content of the appellant's complaint, it was not a letter/visit matter as defined in the Regulations on Letters and Visits, but rather a request for the respondent to stop the pollution of the river channel and investigate and handle it in accordance with the law. This request fell within the statutory duties of the respondent. Therefore, the respondent, the People's Government of Jiashan County, erroneously characterized the appellant's complaint as a letter/visit complaint and, based on the Regulations on Letters and Visits, concluded that the conditions for the appellant's reconsideration application had not yet been satisfied, and accordingly dismissed the appellant's application for administrative reconsideration. This decision was based on unclear facts and insufficient evidence, and should be revoked as a matter of law, with an order for a new decision. Although the specific administrative act by the respondent lacked factual and legal basis, the act itself did not cause material damage to the appellant's interests. Therefore, the appellant's claim for administrative compensation lacked factual and legal basis and was not supported. Accordingly, on August 2, 2013, the Zhejiang High People's Court rendered the administrative judgment ([2013] Zhe Xing Zhong Zi No. 115), dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

(3) Typical Significance

The administrative act sued in this case is the administrative reconsideration decision of Jiashan County Government, but the substantive dispute focus is whether the Jiashan County Environmental Protection Bureau performed its statutory duty of environmental protection in accordance with the law. In recent years, as environmental protection concepts have become deeply rooted in the hearts of the people, the number of complaints and reports from the public concerning environmental violations such as illegal discharge of sewage and exhaust has increased continuously. However, some administrative organs with supervisory and administrative responsibilities for environmental protection have a weak awareness of performing their duties according to law; some ignore the complaints and reports of the public, or delay handling them, while others merely transfer the complaints and reports of the public as general letters and visits matters, without any follow-up. The final judgment in this case held that the appellant complained that the relevant unit directly discharged sewage from pig farming and tableware disinfection into the river, causing serious water pollution and resulting in the mass death of fish and pearl mussels farmed by the appellant, thus requesting that the respondent perform its duty to investigate and punish the violation. The content of the appellant's complaint was not within the scope of letters and visits matters as stipulated in the Regulations on Letters and Visits, but rather a request for the respondent to stop the act of polluting the river and to investigate and punish it in accordance with the law. This request fell within the statutory duties of the respondent. Therefore, the respondent, Jiashan County People's Government, still categorized the appellant's complaint as a letters and visits matter and, based on the provisions of the Regulations on Letters and Visits, held that the conditions for the appellant's application for administrative reconsideration had not yet been met, and rejected the appellant's application for administrative reconsideration. This constituted a finding of unclear facts and insufficient evidence. Accordingly, the court rendered a judgment in accordance with the law, revoking the decision and ordering the respondent to make a new one. The gist of this judgment requires the competent administrative organ for environmental protection to correctly distinguish between the matters of letters and visits by administrative counterparts and applications for performance of duties, and to actively perform its statutory duty to supervise and investigate environmental violations. This is of typical significance. It is understood that after the final judgment of the case, the Jiashan County Environmental Protection Bureau investigated and punished the relevant enterprises that illegally discharged pollutants.

5. Zhang Hui and Zhang Gaoping’s Application for Retrial Innocence Compensation to the Zhejiang Higher People’s Court

(1) Basic Facts

Zhang Hui and Zhang Gaoping (Zhang Hui’s uncle), involved in a rape and murder case that occurred in Hangzhou in 2003, were convicted of rape and sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve and 15 years’ imprisonment, respectively. Upon retrial, the Zhejiang Higher People’s Court (hereinafter referred to as Zhejiang High Court) publicly pronounced on March 26, 2013, revoking the original judgments of first and second instances, declaring Zhang Hui and Zhang Gaoping innocent. On May 2, 2013, Zhang Hui and Zhang Gaoping respectively submitted state compensation applications to the Zhejiang High Court, requesting a total compensation of RMB 2.66 million, including RMB 1.2 million for personal freedom compensation, RMB 1.2 million for mental distress damages, RMB 160,000 for property losses, and RMB 100,000 for legal fees.

(2) Judgment

The Zhejiang High Court, upon review, held that Zhang Hui and Zhang Gaoping were criminally detained from May 23, 2003, to March 26, 2013, when they were exonerated upon retrial, each being deprived of personal freedom for 3,596 days. The court should compensate each for personal freedom in accordance with the statutory standard, and also determine mental distress damages by comprehensively considering the specific circumstances of their wrongful conviction and sentencing, execution of punishment, and impact on their work and life. Accordingly, on May 17, 2013, the court issued a state compensation decision, awarding Zhang Hui and Zhang Gaoping RMB 655,730.6 each for personal freedom compensation and RMB 450,000 each for mental distress damages.

(3) Typical Significance

This case was a criminal wrongful conviction compensation case that attracted high attention from all sectors of society in 2013. During the trial and after the compensation decision was made, major media and websites tracked and commented on it. The Zhejiang Higher People’s Court, as the compensation obligor, while granting compensation in a timely and adequate manner according to law, also actively provided humanitarian compensation and relief in response to Zhang Hui and Zhang Gaoping’s applications for hardship assistance. The uncle and nephew accepted the judgment and did not apply to the Compensation Committee of the Supreme People’s Court for a state compensation decision.

1. Timely Compensation According to Law, Allowing Fairness and Justice to Be Achieved Efficiently. To promptly realize the legitimate rights and interests of the compensation claimant, the State Compensation Law sets a two-month deadline for the compensation obligor’s self-compensation procedure. In this case, the Zhejiang High Court, on the one hand, publicly apologized to Zhang Hui and Zhang Gaoping immediately after the retrial verdict, and on the other hand, filed the case and sent personnel to listen to their opinions on the same day it received the compensation application. Fifteen days later, on the day the Supreme People’s Court issued the Notice on the Standard of Compensation for Violations of Citizens’ Personal Freedom Rights in State Compensation Decisions Made in 2013, it rendered the state compensation decision, protecting their legitimate rights and interests in a timely manner according to law. The social response was generally positive, with netizens and legal professionals commenting that “quick compensation is also a form of justice” and “quick compensation is also a consolation for the wrongfully convicted.”

2. Adequate Compensation According to Law, Reflecting People-Oriented Judicial Care. To adapt to the level of China’s economic and social development, the State Compensation Law implements statutory compensation, only calculating compensation for items that fall within the statutory scope and meet the statutory conditions according to statutory standards, with exceptional items such as mental distress damages allowing discretion. In this case, the Zhejiang High Court determined from the outset the working approach of making full use of existing laws and regulations. For compensation requests falling within the scope of state compensation, it determined personal freedom compensation according to statutory standards, and, based on the local economic development level and the specific circumstances of Zhang Hui and Zhang Gaoping’s wrongful conviction and sentencing, execution of punishment, and impact on work and life, appropriately determined mental distress damages, reflecting people-oriented judicial care.

3. Close Cohesion of “Reversal, Compensation, and Relief,” Achieving an Organic Unity of Legal and Social Effects. During the retrial of this case, the Zhejiang High Court formulated a preliminary state compensation plan and a compensation and relief plan based on the progress of the case. After the retrial verdict of innocence and Zhang Hui and Zhang Gaoping’s submission of state compensation applications, the state compensation work was promptly initiated and concluded in a timely manner, and the issue of compensation and relief was also studied simultaneously and carried out intensively, especially during the later stage of compensation handling and after the case was concluded. The three tasks were closely linked, effectively facilitating Zhang Hui and Zhang Gaoping’s acceptance of the judgment and cessation of litigation, achieving an organic unity of legal and social effects, and serving as a leading example for the handling of other wrongful conviction compensation cases.

6. Yu Enhui, Li Zan, and Li Qian v. Southwest Hospital of Chongqing — Retrial of Medical Damage Compensation Dispute

(1) Basic Facts

Li Anfu (husband of Yu Enhui, father of Li Zan and Li Qian), a resident of Chongqing, sought treatment at the Southwest Hospital of Chongqing on July 22, 2009, due to lower back pain and discomfort, and was hospitalized based on the hospital’s diagnosis. On July 24, 2009, during pre-operative examinations, the Southwest Hospital of Chongqing discovered that the patient showed signs of infection, and thus administered medical measures such as anti-infection treatment and albumin supplementation. However, Li Anfu’s condition gradually worsened and developed into a lung infection. On July 31, 2009, after a hospital-wide consultation, Li Anfu was diagnosed with sepsis and transferred to the infectious disease department for continued treatment, with the hospital issuing a critical illness notice. Li Anfu’s condition further deteriorated, and on August 2, 2009, he developed multiple organ dysfunction syndrome. On August 9, 2009, Li Anfu died despite rescue efforts, with the death diagnosis being: multiple organ dysfunction syndrome, septicopyemia, bilateral pneumonia, and right ankle soft tissue infection. After judicial appraisal, it was determined that Li Anfu’s cause of death was septicopyemia secondary to systemic multiple organ failure, mainly related to his personal constitution; the medical conduct of Southwest Hospital of Chongqing had certain fault, and there was a certain causal relationship with the patient’s death, constituting secondary liability. Southwest Hospital of Chongqing should bear 40% of the compensation liability for the losses caused by Li Anfu’s death.

Yu Enhui, Li Zan, and Li Qian filed a lawsuit with the Shapingba District People’s Court of Chongqing, requesting that Southwest Hospital of Chongqing pay medical expenses of RMB 48,843.27 (including RMB 16,200 for human albumin), death damages of RMB 236,235, and other expenses, totaling RMB 374,953.77.

(2) Judgment

The Supreme People’s Court held upon retrial that the original judgment’s failure to support the claims of Yu Enhui, Li Zan, and Li Qian for human albumin expenses constituted an error in fact-finding. According to the medical records of Southwest Hospital of Chongqing, 20 bottles of human albumin used by Li Anfu were purchased by Yu Enhui, Li Zan, and Li Qian from other sources, and Southwest Hospital of Chongqing also admitted this fact and provided evidence showing that the selling price of each bottle of human albumin at Southwest Hospital of Chongqing was RMB 360. Although Yu Enhui, Li Zan, and Li Qian could not provide the payment receipts for their purchase of human albumin, they explicitly expressed their acceptance of the selling price of human albumin provided by Southwest Hospital of Chongqing, which was significantly lower than the expenses they claimed. Therefore, RMB 7,200 (20 bottles x RMB 360/bottle = RMB 7,200) of the RMB 16,200 claimed for human albumin expenses should be included in the medical expenses incurred during Li Anfu’s hospitalization. The total medical expenses for Li Anfu should be RMB 39,843.27, and Southwest Hospital of Chongqing should bear compensation liability for the above medical expenses according to its degree of fault. In this case, no medical accident appraisal was conducted for the medical conduct of Southwest Hospital of Chongqing. Yu Enhui, Li Zan, and Li Qian’s claim for death damages against Southwest Hospital of Chongqing should be governed by the General Principles of the Civil Law. The Interpretation of the Supreme People’s Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Personal Injury Compensation Cases, which was formulated based on the General Principles of the Civil Law and came into effect on May 1, 2004, contains clear provisions on the scope of application and calculation standards for death damages. Therefore, death damages should be calculated in accordance with the provisions, and then the amount to be borne by Southwest Hospital of Chongqing should be determined based on its degree of fault. The original judgment, which held that Yu Enhui, Li Zan, and Li Qian’s claim for death damages had no legal basis, constituted an error in the application of law and was modified by the court in accordance with the law. The Supreme People’s Court modified the judgment, ordering Southwest Hospital of Chongqing to pay 40% of the death damages of RMB 236,235, i.e., RMB 94,494, to Yu Enhui, Li Zan, and Li Qian.

(3) Typical Significance

This case involves people’s livelihood issues. Any detail can affect whether the legitimate rights and interests of rights holders can be effectively remedied. Accurately determining facts is the foundation for correctly hearing a case. Evidence materials should be comprehensively reviewed and cannot be handled simplistically. Only in this way can formalistic errors be avoided. Whether a claim can be supported requires evidence, but the understanding of the statutory constituent elements of evidence cannot be rigid. Original payment receipts are indeed direct and powerful evidence to prove the quantity and price of goods, but being confined only to this cannot solve complex problems and makes it difficult for the people to feel fairness and justice in every judicial case. The original judgment’s outright denial of Yu Enhui, Li Zan, and Li Qian’s claim for RMB 16,200 for human albumin expenses committed such an error. The 20 bottles of human albumin at issue were administered as prescribed by the doctor at Southwest Hospital of Chongqing. After the doctor issued the prescription, it was given to the patient’s family members for external purchase, and the hospital nurses had injection records. Although Yu Enhui, Li Zan, and Li Qian could not provide original payment receipts, they provided a reasonable explanation for this. Moreover, the actual acquisition cost they originally claimed was far higher than the selling price at Southwest Hospital of Chongqing, but for the sake of a quick resolution of the dispute, they made concessions during the litigation and agreed to calculate their expenditure based on the selling price at Southwest Hospital of Chongqing. Furthermore, Southwest Hospital of Chongqing also provided evidence showing that the price of human albumin it sold during the same period was RMB 360 per bottle. Under these circumstances, the amount of expenses for human albumin purchased by Li Anfu himself during his hospitalization was established by a complete chain of evidence, which satisfied the preponderance of evidence principle for fact-finding in the trial of civil cases. Therefore, the Supreme People’s Court partially supported Yu Enhui, Li Zan, and Li Qian’s claim for human albumin expenses, correcting the error in fact-finding in the original judgment.

In addition, neither Yu Enhui’s side nor Southwest Hospital of Chongqing applied for medical accident appraisal. Therefore, this case should be governed by the General Principles of the Civil Law and the relevant provisions on death damages in the Interpretation of the Supreme People’s Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Personal Injury Compensation Cases. The original judgment, which applied the Regulations on the Handling of Medical Accidents and completely rejected the claim for death damages, also had the problem of improper application of law. The Supreme People’s Court corrected this in the retrial judgment.

7. Nanping Federation of Trade Unions v. Nanping Boji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — Enforcement of Dispute over House Demolition Resettlement Compensation

(1) Basic Facts

In the case of the dispute over house demolition resettlement compensation between the Nanping Federation of Trade Unions and Nanping Boji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., the Yanping District People’s Court of Nanping City, Fujian Province, rendered Civil Judgment (2011) Nan Min Zhong Zi No. 412: 1. Nanping Boji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of the judgment, deliver to the Nanping Federation of Trade Unions the entire floor of the fifth floor of Building 2, Yanfu Haoting, No. 36 Fuqian Road, Nanping City (originally the fifth floor of the podium of Buildings 2, 3, and 4, Nanping Fortune Plaza). 2. Nanping Boji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of the judgment, pay the Nanping Federation of Trade Unions overdue resettlement compensation of RMB 2,887,026. 3. All other claims of the Nanping Federation of Trade Unions are rejected.

After the judgment became effective, Nanping Boji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. failed to perform the obligation to pay as specified in the effective legal instrument. On November 1, 2011, the Nanping Federation of Trade Unions applied to the Yanping District Court for compulsory execution, and the court filed the case for execution on the same day.

(2) Execution

After the case was filed for execution, the Yanping District Court issued an execution notice to the judgment debtor, Nanping Boji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and subsequently froze the bank accounts and some of the properties under the name of the judgment debtor, Nanping Boji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. The executing court organized negotiations between the parties on the delivery of the property and the overdue resettlement compensation. However, the judgment debtor, Nanping Boji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., had already arranged for over 200 square meters of the fifth floor of Building 2, Yanfu Haoting to be used as community office space by the Yanfu Community Neighborhood Committee of Sihe Street, Yanping District. The Yanfu Community Neighborhood Committee moved into the premises after decoration, believing that the community office space was obtained in accordance with regulations and unwilling to move out. For this reason, the over 200 square meters of property that should have been delivered to the Nanping Federation of Trade Unions could not be delivered, and the execution of the case fell into a deadlock.

Thereafter, the executing court organized multiple rounds of negotiations between the parties and lawfully took a series of measures against the judgment debtor, Nanping Boji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., including sealing up properties, freezing accounts, imposing a fine of RMB 500,000, and inviting people’s congress deputies, members of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference, representatives of the public, and media to publicly evaluate the judgment debtor’s refusal to perform its obligations under the effective legal instrument. However, these measures still had no effect.

In October 2013, after the implementation of the Provisions of the Supreme People’s Court on Publishing the List of Dishonest Persons Subject to Enforcement, the executing court, in accordance with these provisions, listed the judgment debtor, Nanping Boji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., in the first batch of the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement, which was published nationwide. The company faced consequences such as social disapproval, increased difficulty in participating in bidding projects, reduced bank credit, and financial institutions’ refusal to support its loans. Under the powerful deterrent of credit sanctions, the company immediately delivered all 1,870.2 square meters of the subject matter of execution to the applicant, the Nanping Federation of Trade Unions, and additionally provided renovated office space for the Yanfu Community Neighborhood Committee. The three parties voluntarily reached an execution settlement agreement on November 25, 2013, thereby resolving the dispute.

(3) Typical Significance

The executing court entered the judgment debtor’s dishonesty information into the Supreme People’s Court’s database of dishonest persons subject to enforcement, publicly disclosed it to society, and at the same time, reported the list information of dishonest persons subject to enforcement to relevant entities in a targeted manner. The entities receiving the report applied credit sanctions to the dishonest persons subject to enforcement in areas such as government procurement, bidding, administrative approval, government support, financing credit, market access, and qualification recognition. The publication and application of the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement, driven by pressure from various aspects to restore their reputation in economic dealings and ensure that their business operations were not affected, compelled the judgment debtor to proactively perform its obligations under the effective legal instrument to the executing court, thereby achieving the purpose of promoting execution and obtaining good social results. The credit sanction function of the system of publishing the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement was effectively utilized.
